title.narrative: Scaling inclusive and accountable climate finance for resilient communities in Kisumu County

description.narrative: Suswatch Kenya proposes to implement the Scaling Inclusive and Accountable Climate Finance for Resilient Communities in Kisumu County project, aimed at strengthening inclusive, transparent, and accountable climate finance governance systems that empower communities especially women, youth, and marginalized groups to actively engage in and benefit from climate action. The project builds on insights and successes from earlier implemented climate finance projects, aiming to strengthen locally led climate action by tackling ongoing challenges such as low community participation, weak institutional coordination, limited transparency and accountability in climate finance management, and inadequate public access to climate finance information in Kisumu County Kisumu County faces increasingly severe climate-related risks such as flooding, drought, and environmental degradation, all of which are intensified by rapid urbanization, deforestation, weak infrastructure, and high poverty levels. Although Kenya’s climate finance framework such as the Financing Locally Led Climate Action (FLLoCA) program offers an opportunity to build resilience at the ward level, local communities often lack the capacity, awareness, and access needed to fully participate in these processes. Marginalized groups, including women, youth, and persons with disabilities, remain underrepresented in climate governance structures and decision-making platforms. This project aims to close these gaps by focusing on three interconnected outcomes: (1) Enhanced transparency and accountability in climate finance governance in Kisumu County; (2) Strengthened institutional capacity and stakeholder collaboration; and (3) Increased meaningful participation of women, youth, and marginalized groups in climate governance structures and decision-making processes in policy engagement. By achieving these goals, the project will ensure that climate funds are not only allocated more effectively but are also equitably distributed based on community priorities and vulnerabilities.
